channel.title: Long Island Business News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Long Island Business News (libn.com)

item.title: Huntington medical office property trades for $3.4M
item.description: A2 Development Group purchased the Village East Professional Center in Huntington for $3.4 million, marking its second office property acquisition in three months.

item.title: Hofstra alum and former Marcum CEO Jeffrey Weiner gives $5M to university
item.description: Jeffrey Weiner, Hofstra alum and former Marcum CEO, donates $5 million to create the Jeffrey M. Weiner Institute for Professional Services at Hofstra University.

item.title: Sam’s Japanese BBQ & Hot Pot opening in Centereach
item.description: Sam Chen and Amanda Lin open Sam’s Japanese BBQ & Hot Pot in Centereach, featuring traditional barbecue and hot pot dishes in a 6,000-square-foot space.

item.title: On Our Island: SBELIH auxiliary donates $643K; LI charity boxing returns
item.description: SBELIH receives a $643K auxiliary donation; LI Fight for Charity seeks boxers; PSEG marks Engineers Week; Suffolk swears in new correction officers.

item.title: Women executives transform leadership in Long Island banking amid industry shifts
item.description: Women executives are reshaping leadership in Long Island banking, with credit unions leading in female CEOs and evolving corporate cultures supporting gender diversity.

item.title: Court ruling doesn’t dissuade developer from EPCAL quest
item.description: Calverton Aviation & Technology continues pursuit of EPCAL property acquisition after court dismisses most claims against Riverhead town.

item.title: Schaffer: Governor Hochul advances affordability and safety to retain Long Island families
item.description: Governor Hochul focuses on affordability, public safety, and housing to keep Long Island families thriving and secure amid rising costs and risks.

item.title: Benzakein, Sorbara: Succession planning challenges in Long Island commercial real estate
item.description: Long Island commercial real estate faces a growing succession challenge as aging professionals retire and younger talent struggles to stay amid affordability issues.

item.title: Inked: Commercial real estate transactions in Long Island including Commack and Huntington
item.description: Several commercial real estate deals took place in Long Island, including purchases and leases in Commack, Bay Shore, West Islip, and Huntington.

item.title: Long Island aquaculture works to rebound after brutal winter
item.description: Long Island oyster farmers suffered major equipment and crop losses due to severe ice damage in winter.
